question: What is hard filtering in GATK and when is it used instead of VQSR?

args.query: GATK hard filtering definition and when to use instead of VQSR

events.reason: This is a documentation definition question, so search_docs is the right tool.

args.query: GATK hard filtering definition and when to use instead of VQSR

events.preview:
Calling Variants on Sequencing Data — Calling Variants on Sequencing Data > Calling Variants > Filtering Variants
### Filtering Variants

There are several ways

final.answer: Hard filtering applies predefined thresholds to variant annotations, such as allele depth and mapping quality, and flags variants that pass or fail all of the criteria [sarek_vc_theory#h008]. It is mostly useful when calling a few samples and enough data are not available for more sophisticated solutions [sarek_vc_theory#h008]. VQSR is the filtering step applied after joint genotyping [sarek_output#h030], and it needs a larger set of annotations with sufficient variance [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. The observations do not state an explicit rule for choosing hard filtering over VQSR; the link is only implied by the small-dataset conditions above.
